compiled_state.title: [ci-llm-review-runner]: PR review surfaces new finding set each cycle -> reviewer cascade without convergence
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 4c154d1bdfd8750d59fbd96af2049228e71e8071
* **workflow:** .github/workflows/llm-review.yml
* **PR:** #98 (session 2026-05-12 f61f-7e0a remediation)

### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior
PR finalize loop converges. After fixing all blocking findings flagged in cycle N, cycle N+1 should either: (a) approve the PR (no blocking findings), (b) re-flag only the same findings (which then trigger same-failure escalation in PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md), or (c) flag a smaller subset. The DefenseStore protocol (prior-defenses-path) is intended to suppress already-defended findings.

#### Actual Behavior
PR #98 cycle 1 → 1 critical + 3 important (4 findings). User addressed the 1 legitimate finding (Trust boundary) + posted defense comments for the 3 defensible ones.

PR #98 cycle 2 (run 25751125173) after addressing cycle 1: **2 critical + 1 fragile + 5 important = 8 findings**. NEW findings include:
- (false positive) finding 2: claims deduplicate_region_findings does not exist — test passes locally with the same import
- (new surface) finding 4: artifact name injection via branch newlines — only theoretically reachable
- (stale) finding 5: secrets-as-env-vars — same finding as cycle 1; defense comment was posted but not consumed
- (new) findings 6/7: test coverage gaps in the tests just added
- (new) finding 8: documentation gap on the asymmetric logic (now removed — the finding is stale)

Cycle 2 introduced MORE blocking findings than cycle 1. Pattern is divergence rather than convergence.

### 3. Action History
1. Pushed commit 4c154d1b addressing cycle 1 finding 3 + posted defense for findings 1/2/4 as PR comment.
2. Cycle 2 ran (run 25751125173) — found 8 findings, half of which target the test/fix from step 1 + half of which restate / reframe earlier findings (with the defense comment not consumed).
3. Pattern matches existing bug 1348-f163 surface (CI review gate fail mode) but distinct: that's about bypass; this is about non-convergence.

### 5. Skills and Workflows
* Workflow: PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md (bounded loop: same-failure 3x, per-PR max 15)
* Caller: /dso:end-session Step 11 → /dso:sprint Phase 8
* Possible root causes:
  (a) prior-defenses-path artifact not produced on session→main PRs (it's a different workflow than sprint-story-review.yml)
  (b) DefenseStore not consulted when llm-review runs on the session→main PR (only consulted on story branches per epic f61f-7e0a design)
  (c) issue-comment-based defense is not machine-readable by the next review cycle; only resolved review THREADS suppress findings
  (d) reviewer prompts encourage broader scope-expansion per cycle
* Fix sketch: investigate which DefenseStore wiring runs on the session→main PR llm-review job. The epic f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d design was per-story attestation; the session→main PR likely uses a different defense path (or none). If no defense path exists for the session-PR cycle, the reviewer will keep finding new surface every push.

comments.body: Cluster investigation complete. Root causes: RC-A (infra, hits this + d565-805a/a2e9-4227 only): DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE never exported in any .github/workflows/*.yml (runner.py:789 defaults to 1; suppression branches at runner.py:843/894/922 dead in CI) AND mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh invoked at ci.yml:288 with no stdin producer (script reads DEFENSE_RECORD from stdin per review-github-defense-store.sh:91-102). RC-B (reviewer prompt, hits ee3a-43fc/b2ef-cd72/9e84-2b78 only): Verify-Before-Assert rules exist in reviewer-base.md:66-82 and code-reviewer-light.md:75-91 but LLM disregards them; needs structured verification_evidence field + post-LLM validator + rubric anchors. Both RCs are independent but compound. Complexity: COMPLEX (8+ files / 3 subsystems / 2 RCs). Per fix-bug Phase D Step 2 — escalating to epic via /dso:brainstorm. Do NOT proceed to RED test / implementation in this session. Recommended fix bundle ships RC-A (F1+F2+F3) before RC-B (F4+F5+F6).

comments.body:
2026-05-13 — Empirical validation on PR #103 (RC-A defense pipeline shipped + verified):

RC-A is now WORKING end-to-end (DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE counted, defenses fetched, suppression matcher fires) but it does NOT solve this convergence bug. Direct cycle-over-cycle evidence:

| Metric | Cycle 1 | Cycle 2 | Cycle 3 (after 31 DEFENSE_RECORDs posted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Findings | 19 | 33 | 17 |
| Critical | 0 | 4 | 5 |
| Fragile | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| Important | 19 | 27 | 12 |
| Suppression hits | n/a | n/a | 0 (defense-keys didn't match new descriptions) |

Cycle-3 CI run 25768839910 job 75690987293 log:
- `Computed DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE=3 (prior cycles: 2)` — cycle counting correct
- `INFO: cycle 3 — loaded 31 prior defense record(s) for dismissal-memory filter` — defenses loaded
- Finding count dropped 33→17 ONLY because the reviewer didn't re-emit the cycle-2 findings; it generated 17 NEW findings on DIFFERENT line numbers and DIFFERENT concerns (empty-diff PR edge case, /tmp full, mktemp validation — none of which were in cycle 2).

Line-number overlap cycle-2 → cycle-3: ~0 of 17. The reviewer is inventing fresh speculative findings each cycle instead of converging.

Root cause (confirmed): the LLM reviewer prompts (reviewer-base.md, code-reviewer-light.md) do not gate on "re-emit prior findings before raising new ones". The matcher in runner.py:369 (`_suppress_defended_findings`) keys on `(severity, description[:80])` — works correctly on textually-equivalent re-emissions, but cannot match semantically-equivalent but textually-distinct re-statements. The reviewer never tries to re-state — it just thinks of new things.

This is RC-B territory per cluster investigation (ticket ee3a-43fc cluster comment 2026-05-12). Convergence requires reviewer-prompt calibration: (a) a "re-emit prior defended findings if still relevant" gate, (b) a "do not invent speculative findings beyond the diff" gate, or (c) post-LLM dedupe by file+line fingerprint rather than description-text matching.

Action: user manually merging PR #103 to ship RC-A; RC-B follow-up tracks here (this ticket) + the cluster ee3a-43fc/b2ef-cd72/9e84-2b78.
